methodological_rigor.justification: Integrated patient-to-preclinical approach combining patient data analysis, ex vivo tumor-on-chip modeling, single-cell RNA sequencing, and functional validation. Multiple independent TNBC primary samples tested in tumor-on-chip models. Proper controls (ECM-myCAF vs. other CAF populations) and functional assays (SRC inhibition, G0S2 silencing) demonstrating causality. Statistical testing with P-values reported. In vitro validation with multiple TNBC cell lines. Patient sample stratification by chemotherapy response.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Case-control clinical study with mechanistic translation identifying ECM-producing myofibroblasts (ECM-myCAF) as drivers of chemotherapy resistance in TNBC. ECM-myCAF prevalence predicts chemotherapy response in patients: decreased in chemosensitive, unchanged in resistant cases. Identifies SRC/G0S2 axis as target to overcome fibroblast-mediated chemoresistance. Direct clinical relevance to improving TNBC therapeutic outcomes.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive methods for patient sample collection, tumor-on-chip modeling (with adequate detail on microfluidic design), single-cell RNA sequencing, immunofluorescence, flow cytometry, and functional assays. Ethics approval referenced for patient samples. scRNA-seq data likely deposited (GEO accession not mentioned in abstract). Tumor-on-chip methodology clearly described. Some supplementary methods likely more extensive than main manuscript.

novelty_literature.justification: Identifies specific ECM-myCAF subset (not CAF population broadly) as chemotherapy resistance driver, advancing beyond general CAF biology understanding. Mechanistic discovery of SRC activation and G0S2 upregulation as resistance mechanism is novel. Tumor-on-chip integration with patient data represents innovative translational approach. Contributes new understanding of fibroblast-mediated chemotherapy resistance.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-written manuscript with clear introduction to TNBC chemotherapy resistance and CAF heterogeneity. Methods adequately describe complex experimental pipeline from patient samples through tumor-on-chip to molecular validation. Results logically progress from CAF subset identification through mechanistic characterization. Figures effectively communicate key findings (ECM-myCAF prevalence, SRC activation, G0S2 expression). Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings.

key_strengths: Identifies specific ECM-myCAF population (not broad CAF category) as driver of TNBC chemotherapy resistance through patient data analysis
Innovative tumor-on-chip ex vivo modeling validates ECM-myCAF-mediated chemoresistance and enables mechanistic dissection
Mechanistic clarity: ECM-myCAFs activate SRC kinases in TNBC cells, upregulating G0S2 anti-apoptotic regulator; both are targetable
Clinical predictor identified: ECM-myCAF prevalence decreases in chemosensitive but not chemoresistant TNBC, supporting biomarker development
key_concerns: Patient sample size not explicitly stated; statistical power for identifying chemotherapy response correlation not reported
Tumor-on-chip model uses limited number of TNBC cell lines; generalizability to TNBC diversity not fully assessed
SRC and G0S2 inhibitors tested in vitro; in vivo xenograft models with combination chemotherapy not presented
Therapeutic strategy development incomplete; no proposed regimen combining SRC/G0S2 inhibition with chemotherapy
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 2 paper: excellent integrated translational work identifying actionable fibroblast subset and mechanistic vulnerability in TNBC chemotherapy resistance. Requires in vivo validation and clinical biomarker development. Strong foundation for therapeutic translation; appropriate for high-impact oncology journal.
